quick: IR: 60 mg every 4-6 h (max 240 mg/day); ER: 120 mg q12h or 240 mg q24h
With or without food; avoid late doses (insomnia)
Avoid in 1st trimester; use cautiously later, lowest dose
Small amounts in milk; may reduce milk supply - use caution
Reduce dose/extend interval in significant impairment
Blood pressure, heart rate, insomnia, CNS stimulation
summary: Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic amine used as an oral decongestant for nasal and sinus congestion from colds and allergic rhinitis. It stimulates alpha-adrenergic receptors on respiratory mucosal blood vessels, causing vasoconstriction and reduced mucosal edema, with some beta activity. Common effects include hypertension, tachycardia and insomnia; because it is a precursor for methamphetamine synthesis, its sale is legally restricted.
indications: Temporary relief of nasal and sinus congestion due to the common cold, hay fever or other upper respiratory allergies
Relief of eustachian tube congestion / ear pressure

dosage.n: Max 120 mg/day; not recommended under 4 years

admin: Take with a full glass of water; with or without food
Avoid doses close to bedtime to reduce insomnia
Swallow extended-release products whole - do not crush, chew or split
Do not exceed the maximum daily dose
Sold from behind the pharmacy counter with purchase quantity/ID restrictions in many jurisdictions
moa: Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic that acts both directly on alpha-adrenergic receptors and indirectly by releasing norepinephrine. Alpha-stimulation constricts dilated blood vessels in the nasal and sinus mucosa, reducing engorgement, edema and secretion to relieve congestion. Mild beta activity can increase heart rate and bronchodilation.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to pseudoephedrine or sympathomimetic amines
Use within 14 days of an MAO inhibitor (hypertensive crisis)
Severe hypertension or severe coronary artery disease

preg: Avoid in the first trimester (association with gastroschisis reported); if used later in pregnancy, use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time and avoid in women with hypertension.
lact: Excreted into breast milk in small amounts; may decrease milk production. Use with caution, prefer single doses, and watch the infant for irritability.
renal: Renally eliminated; reduce the dose or extend the dosing interval in significant renal impairment, where the half-life is prolonged.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: MAO inhibitors - risk of hypertensive crisis (contraindicated within 14 days)
moderate: Antihypertensives (e.g., beta-blockers, methyldopa, reserpine) - reduced antihypertensive effect / pressor response
Other sympathomimetics/stimulants - additive cardiovascular and CNS effects
minor: Antacids - increased absorption rate; urinary acidifiers - increased clearance
interactions.food: No major food interaction; avoid late dosing to prevent insomnia.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; possible additive cardiovascular/CNS effects.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise blood pressure and heart rate; can interfere with urine catecholamine/amphetamine immunoassays (false positives).

monitoring: Blood pressure and heart rate, especially in cardiovascular disease or hypertension
Symptom improvement; reassess if no relief within 7 days or if fever develops
Urinary symptoms in men with prostatic enlargement
counsel: Do not take late in the day - it can keep you awake
Do not use if you take or recently stopped an MAOI antidepressant
If you have high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid problems, diabetes or trouble urinating, check before using
Stop and seek advice if you get a fast/pounding heart, severe headache or nervousness
Do not use more than directed; see a doctor if symptoms last more than 7 days or come with fever
pk: Decongestion within about 30 minutes of an oral dose
Plasma peak about 1-3 hours (later for extended-release)
Approximately 5-8 hours (longer with alkaline urine or renal impairment)
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from moisture and light
pearls: Sale is legally restricted (kept behind the pharmacy counter, quantity-limited, ID required) because it is a methamphetamine precursor
Common offenders for hypertension and insomnia - avoid evening doses and use cautiously in cardiovascular disease
Contraindicated within 14 days of MAO inhibitors - risk of hypertensive crisis
First-trimester use linked to gastroschisis - generally avoided early in pregnancy
May lower the threshold for urinary retention in men with prostatic enlargement
missed: As a symptom-relief medicine, take a dose when needed for congestion; if on a schedule, skip a missed dose if it is nearly time for the next one. Never take two doses at once or exceed the daily maximum.
overdose: Overdose causes severe hypertension, tachycardia or reflex bradycardia, agitation, hallucinations, sweating, seizures and, rarely, arrhythmias or stroke. Management is supportive: monitoring, sedation with benzodiazepines, and control of blood pressure (avoid unopposed beta-blockade); urinary acidification can enhance elimination but is rarely needed.
